Page: https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/reference/error-codes.html
Source: docs/developer-portal/reference/error-codes.md

# Error code catalogue

[Reference](README.md) · [Full code index (106 codes, generated)](error-code-index.md) · [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting/README.md) · [API overview](../api/README.md#errors)

A Parmana error is an HTTP status plus a body. The body has an `error` message and, for most refusals, a `code`. The SDKs turn the status into a class, and keep the server's code where one is sent.

This page lists the codes a developer meets most often. Each row says whether the code was **observed** in this verification (the status and message are real), or **from source/spec** (the code and status are in the OpenAPI document or the server source, and the row says where). The [generated index](error-code-index.md) lists every code the server source defines, with the file that raises it.

## Status to SDK class

| Status | TypeScript class                                                      | Python class                                      | Notes                                                                              |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400`  | `ValidationError`                                                     | `ValidationError`                                 | Malformed request. Nothing was stored.                                             |
| `401`  | `AuthenticationError`                                                 | `AuthenticationError`                             | No key, or an unknown key.                                                         |
| `403`  | `AuthorizationError`, or `ExecutionRejectedError` for `POLICY_DENIED` | `AuthorizationError`, or `ExecutionRejectedError` | `CAPABILITY_NOT_ALLOWED` and `TENANT_NOT_ALLOWED` keep their code as `serverCode`. |
| `404`  | `NotFoundError`                                                       | `NotFoundError`                                   |                                                                                    |
| `409`  | `ConflictError`                                                       | `ConflictError`                                   |                                                                                    |
| `202`  | `ExecutionPendingError` (on execute)                                  | `ExecutionPendingError`                           | Released; the status is not yet final.                                             |
| `429`  | `RateLimitError`                                                      | `RateLimitError`                                  | `retryAfterSeconds` when `Retry-After` is sent.                                    |
| `5xx`  | `InternalServerError`                                                 | `InternalServerError`                             | The server code is kept as `serverCode`.                                           |
| none   | `NetworkError`, `TimeoutError`                                        | `NetworkError`, `TimeoutError`                    |                                                                                    |

The mapping is in `typescript/src/transport/mapHttpErrorResponse.ts` and in the Python `errors` package.

## Codes observed in this verification

| Code                                   | Status                                                           | Where it comes from                           | Message (as observed)                                                                                   | Meaning and fix                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `CAPABILITY_NOT_ALLOWED`               | `403`                                                            | Caller check on `POST /execute`               | `Caller is not permitted to invoke this capability.`                                                    | The key may not invoke this action. Check `GET /callers/me`.                                                                         |
| `CAPABILITY_NOT_BOUND`                 | `404`                                                            | `GET /policies/in-effect`                     | `No policy is bound to capability "…".`                                                                 | The capability has no policy binding on this build. Name the policy in the request instead.                                          |
| `VERIFICATION_FAILED`                  | `404`                                                            | `POST /verify`, `POST /receipt`               | `Execution Trust Record not found.`                                                                     | The key has no record with that id. Check the id and the key.                                                                        |
| `SAME_ACTOR_CANNOT_APPROVE_OWN_CHANGE` | `403`                                                            | `POST /policies/pending-changes/{id}/approve` | `…was proposed by this same caller — the proposer (maker) may not also approve or reject it (checker).` | The maker tried to approve their own change. A different checker approves.                                                           |
| `NON_HUMAN_CALLER_DENIED`              | `403`                                                            | Governance routes                             | `NON_HUMAN_CALLER_DENIED` (code)                                                                        | A service caller tried a human-only route.                                                                                           |
| `STEP_UP_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID`        | `403`                                                            | Governance approve and reject                 | (code)                                                                                                  | The envelope is missing, expired, wrong, or not signed by the checker's registered key. Sign a fresh envelope and submit it at once. |
| `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`                   | Not captured (the runner reported a business-validation outcome) | A sourced fact                                | `business validation SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE: … payment provider timed out`                                  | The source did not answer. Parmana fails closed. Do not approve on a guess.                                                          |
| `RATE_LIMITED`                         | `429`                                                            | Rate limits                                   | `429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After 60`                                                                  | Too many requests, or too many failed authentications. Wait for `Retry-After`.                                                       |

Plain error bodies without a code are also common. Each row below was observed unless it says "from source":

| Status | Body (observed)                                                                                               | Meaning                                                                                             |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401`  | `{"error":"authentication required"}`                                                                         | No key, or an unknown key.                                                                          |
| `400`  | `{"error":"businessTransactionId must be a valid UUID."}`                                                     | The id is not a UUID.                                                                               |
| `400`  | `{"error":"capability is required, for example ?capability=erp:invoice-pay."}`                                | A required query parameter is missing.                                                              |
| `403`  | `{"error":"Caller is not permitted to assert this authority.principalId."}` (from source, not triggered here) | The key may not act for this principal. No code.                                                    |
| `403`  | `{"error":"Execution rejected: Rejected: …"}`                                                                 | An execution refused by the decision. The message names the reason.                                 |
| `404`  | `{"error":"Business Transaction not found."}`                                                                 | Unknown transaction for this key.                                                                   |
| `404`  | `{"error":"Execution Trust Record not found."}`                                                               | Unknown record.                                                                                     |
| `404`  | `{"error":"Policy 'vendor-payment' version '2.1.0' was not found."}`                                          | No such version on this server.                                                                     |
| `409`  | `{"error":"Business Transaction '…' already exists."}`                                                        | The id was used. Nothing ran again.                                                                 |
| `400`  | `{"error":"Request body must be a Refusal Record (refusalRecordId, …)."}`                                     | A verification body is missing fields. The message names them.                                      |
| `404`  | `{"error":"Route not found.","code":"ROUTE_NOT_FOUND"}`                                                       | An unknown path, sent with a valid key. Added in this change; earlier builds returned an HTML page. |

### Execution refusals

A refused execution comes back as `403` with a message that begins `Execution rejected:`. The message is the reason. The observed reasons:

| Reason (observed)                                                                                                                            | Cause                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Rejected: policy "vendor-payment"@"2.1.0" has no PolicyChangeApprovalRecord -- it has never completed the Policy Governance approval flow.` | The version was never approved through maker-checker.                                  |
| `Rejected: policy "vendor-payment"@"2.1.0" was superseded: the version in effect is "2.1.1", the one most recently approved.`                | The request named an older version.                                                    |
| `Rejected: declared signal(s) do not match independently verified state (humanApproved=true != verified humanApproved=false).`               | The verified human approval is false: expired, wrong target or amount, or not trusted. |
| `Rejected: declared signal(s) do not match the executed intent (paymentAmount=999 != intent.parameters.amount=1000).`                        | A bound signal differs from the request.                                               |
| `Rejected: no approval verifier is configured, so the signed human approval this action needs cannot be checked.`                            | The server has no approval verifier configured (tutorial 120).                         |
| `Vendor payment rejected because the assessed payment risk exceeds the maximum permitted threshold.`                                         | A policy rule rejected the request.                                                    |
| `Vendor payment rejected because one or more required policy conditions were not satisfied.`                                                 | A required condition is not met, for example no approval attached.                     |

## Codes from source and the OpenAPI document

These were not triggered by a live server run. Each is described from the OpenAPI document (`openapi/openapi.yaml`) or the server source. Where an automated test in the server's suite triggers the branch, the row names that test. The status is the one the document states.

| Code                          | Status                                                                           | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Action                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `POLICY_DENIED`               | `403`                                                                            | The policy refused the request. Final for that request.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Show the reason. Do not retry.                         |
| `EXECUTION_RECORD_INCOMPLETE` | `500`                                                                            | The action was released, but its signed record could not be produced. The OpenAPI document says not to retry as a new transaction. Triggered over HTTP by `packages/api/tests/integration/execution-record-incomplete-http.integration.test.ts` (the response has the code and the transaction id, and the connector ran once). | Reconcile the transaction.                             |
| `EXECUTION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`   | `502`                                                                            | The action was released and the connector call failed. Triggered over HTTP by `packages/api/tests/integration/execution-failure.integration.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                           | Reconcile against the connector. Do not resend as new. |
| `SIGNING_UNAVAILABLE`         | `503`                                                                            | Signing is unavailable. The source describes it as "nothing executed".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Retry later with the same id.                          |
| `TENANT_NOT_ALLOWED`          | `403`                                                                            | The key may not act for this `tenantId`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Use an allowed tenant, or omit it.                     |
| `AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE`           | `503` (in the audit path)                                                        | The caller audit trail could not be written, so the request is refused rather than run unrecorded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Check the database.                                    |
| `EXECUTION_STATUS_PENDING`    | `202`                                                                            | Released and recorded, status `EXECUTING`. Triggered on PostgreSQL by `packages/api/tests/integration/transaction-status-postgres.integration.test.ts` (the EXECUTED write fails after the release).                                                                                                                            | Reconcile.                                             |
| `NO_APPROVAL_RECORD`          | `403` at execution (observed as the refusal "has no PolicyChangeApprovalRecord") | A policy version has no approval record.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Approve the version through maker-checker.             |

The full list of codes the server defines, with the file that raises each, is in the [generated index](error-code-index.md). Many of them are for features that are opt-in or experimental: execution intents (`EXECUTION_INTENT_*`), the kill switch (`KILL_SWITCH_*`), inbound refunds, the policy v2 review and replay flow (`REVIEW_*`, `THRESHOLD_*`), and connector changes. Those are described in the [API overview](../api/README.md#experimental-and-opt-in-routes).

## HTTP status summary

| Status | Typical codes                                                                                                                                                       | First check                                                                              |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `200`  | none                                                                                                                                                                | Read the body. For verify and replay, read `status` or `verified`, not the status alone. |
| `201`  | none                                                                                                                                                                | A proposal or declaration was accepted.                                                  |
| `202`  | `EXECUTION_STATUS_PENDING`                                                                                                                                          | Reconcile. Do not resubmit.                                                              |
| `400`  | none (message names the field)                                                                                                                                      | Fix the request.                                                                         |
| `401`  | none                                                                                                                                                                | Check the key.                                                                           |
| `403`  | `POLICY_DENIED`, `CAPABILITY_NOT_ALLOWED`, `TENANT_NOT_ALLOWED`, `SAME_ACTOR_CANNOT_APPROVE_OWN_CHANGE`, `NON_HUMAN_CALLER_DENIED`, `STEP_UP_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID` | Read the message and the code.                                                           |
| `404`  | `CAPABILITY_NOT_BOUND`                                                                                                                                              | Check the id, the policy version, and the binding.                                       |
| `409`  | none                                                                                                                                                                | The id was used. Read the existing outcome.                                              |
| `429`  | `RATE_LIMITED`                                                                                                                                                      | Wait for `Retry-After`.                                                                  |
| `500`  | `EXECUTION_RECORD_INCOMPLETE`                                                                                                                                       | The action may have run. Reconcile.                                                      |
| `502`  | `EXECUTION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`                                                                                                                                         | The action may have run. Reconcile.                                                      |
| `503`  | `SIGNING_UNAVAILABLE`, `AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE`                                                                                                                          | Nothing was executed. Retry later.                                                       |

For the debugging steps that go with each row, see [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting/README.md).

# Troubleshooting

[Portal home](../README.md) · [Error codes](../reference/error-codes.md) · [FAQ](../faq.md) · [Getting started](../getting-started.md)

This page starts from what you see and works back to the cause. The messages quoted here were observed in this verification, unless a section says otherwise. For the full list of codes, read the [error code reference](../reference/error-codes.md).

**First, find the status and the code.** In the SDKs, read `error.constructor.name`, `error.statusCode` (TypeScript) or `error.status_code` (Python), and the server code (`serverCode` in TypeScript, `server_code` in Python). Over HTTP, read the `code` field of the body.

## Debugging checklist

Run these in order. Each step narrows the cause.

| Step                                | Command                                                                                                                                                              | What a healthy answer looks like                                     |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Is the server up?                | `curl -s $PARMANA_API_URL/health`                                                                                                                                    | `{"status":"UP"}`                                                    |
| 2. Is it ready, and what storage?   | `curl -s $PARMANA_API_URL/ready`                                                                                                                                     | `{"status":"READY", …, "authDisabled":false}`                        |
| 3. Does my key work?                | `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" $PARMANA_API_URL/callers/me`                                                                                                | Your `callerId` and the capabilities you expect                      |
| 4. Is the policy version in effect? | `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "$PARMANA_API_URL/policies/validate" -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"policyId":"…","policyVersion":"…"}'` | `{"valid":true,"errors":[]}`. Then check it is the one you approved. |
| 5. What happened to my transaction? | `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "$PARMANA_API_URL/transactions/$ID/status?history=true"`                                                                    | `current.status` and the history                                     |
| 6. Was it refused?                  | `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" $PARMANA_API_URL/refusal/$ID`                                                                                               | The refusal record, with its `decision`                              |
| 7. Does the record verify?          | The [evidence verification](../security/evidence-verification.md) steps                                                                                              | `valid: true`                                                        |

For the CLI, add `--verbose` to log each request and response code with secrets removed, and `--dry-run` to see the request without sending it. The CLI as an installed bin needs the workaround in [CLI](../sdk/cli.md#the-installed-binary-fixed-in-the-repository-not-yet-in-a-published-release).

## Authentication failures

| Symptom                                    | Cause                                             | Fix                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401 {"error":"authentication required"}`  | No `Authorization` header, or the key is unknown. | Send `Authorization: Bearer <raw key>`. The raw key is what was generated, not its hash. |
| `401` from the SDK (`AuthenticationError`) | The same, seen through the SDK.                   | Check the environment variable is set in the process that runs the code.                 |
| `429` after two `401`s                     | The authentication-failure rate limit.            | Stop retrying with a bad key. Fix the key. Wait for the `Retry-After` window.            |

## Authorization and caller permission failures

| Symptom                                                                                                 | Code                                   | Cause                                                                                           | Fix                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Caller is not permitted to invoke this capability.`                                                    | `CAPABILITY_NOT_ALLOWED`               | The action is not in your key's `allowedCapabilities`.                                          | Ask the operator to add it, or use a key that has it. Check with `GET /callers/me`. |
| `Caller is not permitted to assert this authority.principalId.`                                         | none                                   | The `principalId` is not in your key's `allowedPrincipalIds`.                                   | Use an allowed principal.                                                           |
| `Caller is not permitted to act for this tenantId.`                                                     | `TENANT_NOT_ALLOWED`                   | The `tenantId` is not allowed for your key.                                                     | Use an allowed tenant, or leave it out.                                             |
| `…was proposed by this same caller — the proposer (maker) may not also approve or reject it (checker).` | `SAME_ACTOR_CANNOT_APPROVE_OWN_CHANGE` | A maker tried to approve their own change.                                                      | A different, listed checker approves.                                               |
| `403 NON_HUMAN_CALLER_DENIED`                                                                           | `NON_HUMAN_CALLER_DENIED`              | A service caller tried a human-only route.                                                      | Use a human's key for governance routes.                                            |
| `403 STEP_UP_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID`                                                                     | `STEP_UP_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID`        | The step-up envelope is missing, expired, wrong, or not signed by the checker's registered key. | Sign a fresh envelope with the checker's step-up key, and submit it at once.        |

## Policy evaluation failures

| Symptom                                                                                                              | Code                              | Cause                                                                                                                 | Fix                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Policy 'vendor-payment' version '2.1.0' was not found.`                                                             | none (`404`)                      | The version is not on this server.                                                                                    | Check the name and version. Check `PARMANA_POLICY_DIR`.                                                                             |
| `No policy is bound to capability "…".`                                                                              | `CAPABILITY_NOT_BOUND` (`404`)    | The capability has no policy binding on this build. The test capability `test:fixture-execute` is unbound on purpose. | Name the policy and version in `policy` (as the examples do). A capability needs a binding for `GET /policies/in-effect` to answer. |
| `…was superseded: the version in effect is "2.1.1", the one most recently approved.`                                 | (`403`, `ExecutionRejectedError`) | You named a version that is no longer the one in effect.                                                              | Name the version in effect. See [Policy management](../policies/README.md#versions-and-the-version-in-effect).                      |
| `…has no PolicyChangeApprovalRecord -- it has never completed the Policy Governance approval flow.`                  | (`403`, `ExecutionRejectedError`) | The version was never approved through maker-checker. On a fresh server this is the normal first state.               | Approve the version. See [Maker-checker](../tutorials/maker-checker.md).                                                            |
| `Vendor payment rejected because the assessed payment risk exceeds the maximum permitted threshold.`                 | `POLICY_DENIED` (`403`)           | A policy rule rejected the request.                                                                                   | The reason is the policy's own. Show it. Do not retry the same request.                                                             |
| `Vendor payment rejected because one or more required policy conditions were not satisfied.`                         | `POLICY_DENIED` (`403`)           | A required condition is not met, for example no approval was attached.                                                | Attach the approval, or supply the required facts.                                                                                  |
| `declared signal(s) do not match the executed intent (paymentAmount=999 != intent.parameters.amount=1000).`          | (`403`)                           | A bound signal differs from the request.                                                                              | Build both values from the same variable.                                                                                           |
| `declared signal(s) do not match independently verified state (humanApproved=true != verified humanApproved=false).` | (`403`)                           | Parmana's independent check of the approval returned false.                                                           | See [Approval failures](#approval-failures).                                                                                        |

### Approval failures

An approval is refused when Parmana cannot verify it for this request. The message names the signal that failed, which is `humanApproved` in the examples. Causes observed in this verification:

| Cause                                                         | Observed result                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No approval attached, and `humanApproved` is false            | A policy-condition refusal (`POLICY_DENIED`).                                                      |
| The approval's `ttlSeconds` has passed                        | `humanApproved` verified as false.                                                                 |
| The approval names a different target (`resourceId`)          | `humanApproved` verified as false.                                                                 |
| The approval's `maxAmount` is below the amount requested      | `humanApproved` verified as false.                                                                 |
| The approval was signed by a key the server does not trust    | `humanApproved` verified as false (or the server reports that no approval verifier is configured). |
| The approval is reused                                        | A second use is refused.                                                                           |
| The approval is attached to a transaction declared without it | Refused on execution. An approval cannot be added to a declared transaction.                       |

Check, in order: the approval's `capability` equals the intent's action; `resourceId` equals the target; `maxAmount` covers the amount; the approval has not expired; the approver's key is trusted by the server (`approverId` and `keyId` match the registered approver); the approval was not used before.

## Duplicates and status failures

| Symptom                                    | Code                             | Meaning                                                  | What to do                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Business Transaction '…' already exists.` | `409`                            | The `businessTransactionId` was used. Nothing ran again. | Read the existing outcome: `trustRecord()` or `transactionStatus()`. Use a new id only for a new action. |
| `202` with `status: EXECUTING`             | (`202`, `ExecutionPendingError`) | Released and recorded, but the status is not yet final.  | Call `reconcileTransaction`. Do not resubmit.                                                            |
| `500` `EXECUTION_RECORD_INCOMPLETE`        | `EXECUTION_RECORD_INCOMPLETE`    | Released; the signed record could not be produced.       | Reconcile. Do not retry as a new transaction.                                                            |
| `502` `EXECUTION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`          | `EXECUTION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`      | Released; the connector call failed.                     | Reconcile against the connector.                                                                         |
| `503` `SIGNING_UNAVAILABLE`                | `SIGNING_UNAVAILABLE`            | Signing is unavailable. Nothing was executed.            | Retry later, with the same id.                                                                           |

## Signature and verification failures

These are the messages the verifiers print (observed):

| Message                                                                                                                   | Meaning                                                               | What to check                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trustRecordHash mismatch: expected …`                                                                                    | A covered field of the record differs from what was signed.           | The record was changed, or was reformatted with a changed value. Use the original.                                              |
| `signature verification failed for keyId "default" (ed25519).`                                                            | The signature does not verify with the key in your trust file.        | The record was altered, or it was signed by another key. Compare the fingerprint.                                               |
| `schemaVersion 2 (or no schemaVersion) covers only seven top-level fields and is refused by default: set allowLegacyV2 …` | A schema 2 record, and the trust file does not accept it.             | Set `allowLegacyV2` knowingly, or verify a schema 3 record. See [Security](../security/README.md#schema-versions-and-coverage). |
| `record has no hybrid envelope: set hybridRequiredFrom or allowLegacyOnly …`                                              | A single-signature record, and the trust file does not accept it.     | Set `allowLegacyOnly` knowingly, or verify a hybrid record.                                                                     |
| `valid: true` with `coverage: legacy`                                                                                     | The record verified, but only its seven covered fields are protected. | Read the security page before relying on uncovered fields.                                                                      |

## Network and timeout failures

| Symptom       | SDK class        | Cause                                                | What to do                                                                                  |
| ------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No response   | `NetworkError`   | The endpoint is unreachable, or a proxy blocked it.  | Check the endpoint, DNS and proxy. Read the status before any retry.                        |
| Slow response | `TimeoutError`   | The request exceeded `timeout` (default 30 seconds). | Check the status of the transaction. The action may have been released. Do not resubmit it. |
| `429`         | `RateLimitError` | The rate limit was reached.                          | Wait for `retryAfterSeconds`. Reduce the request rate.                                      |

The SDK retries `GET` requests only, when retries are enabled. It never retries a `POST`. A `POST` that timed out may still have run: read the transaction's status before you decide.

## Problems with the existing quickstart and local setup

These were found when the existing [quickstart](../../../docs/site/quickstart.mdx) was run as written on a fresh checkout. They are recorded in [COVERAGE](../COVERAGE.md#known-issues-found-during-this-review). The governed setup in [Getting started](../getting-started.md) avoids each one.

### The existing quickstart did not run as written (now corrected)

These were the problems in the quickstart. The quickstart page and the code are corrected in this change; the list stays so that anyone who followed an older copy can match the error to its fix.

1. **The server refused to start without `PARMANA_POLICY_DIR`.** Fixed: the quickstart's server command sets `PARMANA_POLICY_DIR=./fixtures/policies`.
2. **The server refused to start without `PARMANA_KEY_DIR`.** Fixed: the command sets `PARMANA_KEY_DIR=./keys`. The setting is required in every environment, including `NODE_ENV=test`.
3. **The approver key generator did not create its output folder.** Fixed: `generate-approver-key` creates the folder, so no `mkdir` is needed.
4. **The first execution is refused until the policy is approved.** Still true, and deliberate: `vendor-payment@2.1.0` has no approval record on a fresh server. The quickstart now says so and points to the maker-checker flow. It is not automated (see [FINDINGS](../FINDINGS.md), F7).
5. **`PARMANA_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED_POLICY=true` did nothing.** Fixed: the setting is removed from the examples runner, the load test and tutorial 81. Governance is enforced in every environment.

### `npm run dev:setup` refuses the fixture flows

`npm run dev:setup` starts a server with `PARMANA_POLICY_DIR=./policies`, which does not include `vendor-payment`. Its caller key can invoke only `test:fixture-execute`, which is unbound by design. Verified: `POST /execute` for `vendor-payment@2.1.0` returns `404 Policy 'vendor-payment' version '2.1.0' was not found.`, and `GET /policies/in-effect?capability=test:fixture-execute` returns `404 CAPABILITY_NOT_BOUND`. Use the governed setup for the fixture flows.

### Hybrid signing without a secondary provider (now refused at start-up)

Earlier builds released the action and then returned `500` with `Secondary signature provider is not configured.` The server now refuses to start with `CRYPTO_MODE=hybrid` unless `SECONDARY_SIGNATURE_PROVIDER` is set and differs from the primary, and it checks the secondary key files before it binds the port. If you see a `500` like this on an older build, reconcile the released transaction and do not resubmit it. Set `SECONDARY_SIGNATURE_PROVIDER=dilithium3`, with a `default-secondary` key in the key directory. See [Security](../security/README.md#schema-versions-and-coverage).

### A policy file does not match its approval record

The server refuses a policy whose file was changed outside the approval flow. The message, as the existing [troubleshooting guide](../../../docs/site/troubleshooting.mdx) describes it, names the content hash. This message was not reproduced in this verification. Restore the file to the approved content, or propose the new content through maker-checker.

## Debugging the CLI

- The published `parmana-ops` 4.1.1 printed nothing and exited 0 when run under its bin name. The fix is in the repository and is not yet in a published release. Until then run the file: `node "$(npm root -g)/@parmana/cli/dist/index.js" --help`. See [CLI](../sdk/cli.md#the-installed-binary-fixed-in-the-repository-not-yet-in-a-published-release).
- A `HTTP 403 SAME_ACTOR…` from `approval submit` with the hint "This token is not allowed to do this. Check which credential is set." means the token in `PARMANA_TOKEN` is the maker's, not the checker's.

## Tests and examples that fail on a fresh checkout

- **`npm test --workspace=typescript` failed** before this change: six test files were empty and the integration suites needed the root test setup. Fixed: the empty files are removed, and the workspace script runs with the root configuration. It passes with no extra environment (22 files, 248 tests).
- **Tutorials 60, 103 and 120 need `PARMANA_POLICY_DIR`** (and 103 also `PARMANA_KEY_DIR`) when run directly. Their READMEs now state the command. `npm run examples` sets these defaults for you.
- **`DATABASE_URL` in your environment** can make a test run target a database. The repository's test setup refuses hosted databases unless they are listed in `PARMANA_TEST_PROJECT_REFS` and `ALLOW_LIVE_SUPABASE=1` is set. Unset `DATABASE_URL` for local runs.

## Getting more help

- Open an issue in the repository with the status, the code, the request id if the server gave one, and the output of the debugging checklist. Do not include raw keys, approver private keys or step-up private keys.
- Report a security issue through [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/pavancharak/parmana-core/blob/main/SECURITY.md), not in a public issue.

# Changelog

[Portal home](README.md) · [Coverage report](COVERAGE.md)

This changelog records changes to the developer portal in `docs/developer-portal/`. It does not record changes to the Parmana software. For those, see the repository's release notes and the packages' own changelogs (for example `parmana-verifier`'s `CHANGELOG.md`).

Versions follow the packages the portal documents: SDKs and server 4.1.1, offline verifier 2.0.3.

## 2026-11-20: execution system defects fixed; publishing decided

- The placeholder `DefaultExecutionSystem` is renamed `SimulatedExecutionSystem`, and documented as executing nothing. All references are updated. The name is kept only in historical records.
- `HttpExecutionSystem` applies its `timeout` option with `AbortSignal.timeout`, and says the action may have run.
- `HttpExecutionSystem` checks each response field before returning the result.
- Both packages are decided public. `@parmana/envelope-verifier` is added to the release process; `@parmana/execution-system` is held until its receiving-system obligations are documented. Nothing is published.
- New API references: `packages/envelope-verifier-api.md` and `packages/execution-system-api.md`.

## 2026-11-20: schema version 3 is the default

The owner made schema 3 the default: an unset `HYBRID_SCHEMA_VERSION` now means 3, and `2` is the rollback. The acknowledgement gate (`HYBRID_SCHEMA_V3_ACKNOWLEDGED`) is no longer read. This applies only to hybrid signing: a server in `CRYPTO_MODE=single` issues no schema 3 records. Changed: the parser and the doctor check, the tests that encoded the old default (each now states the schema it signs), `.env.example`, the public environment table, and the portal pages. Receipts are unchanged. The owner reports no active consumer and no single-mode record.

## 2026-11-20: schema version 3 documented in full

Added [Schema version 3](security/schema-v3.md): what v3 covers and what it does not, the server and verifier settings, the downgrade decision and its cutover instant (`2026-11-20T13:01:38Z`), the issuance gate with its evidence, and the rollout and rollback steps. The code default is unchanged.

## 2026-11-20: third pass: the review items with a non-breaking fix

Applied the fixes the review asked for that do not change existing behaviour. Each has a test.

- **Python SDK:** `client.server_version()` asks the server for its version, as the TypeScript `version()` does. `client.version` stays the SDK version. (FINDINGS F4)
- **Both SDKs:** the offline trust-record check takes an opt-in `requireFullCoverage` (TypeScript) or `require_full_coverage=True` (Python). It fails closed on legacy (schema 2) records. The default result is unchanged. (FINDINGS F2)
- **Python samples:** the generated Policy v2 samples run their request only under `__main__`. Pytest collects files named `*_test.py`, and an import-time request reached the network during collection.
- **Portal checker:** counts SDK methods from padded table rows too. Before this, the count depended on how the index was last formatted.
- **Cleanup:** removed two empty, unreferenced fixtures (`typescript/test/fixtures/policy.ts` and `replay-result.ts`).

Still open, and needing an owner decision or a release: the schema 2 default (F1), the approval helper for the quickstart (F7), and publishing the `parmana-ops` entry-point fix (the published 4.1.1 still has the old check).

## 2026-11-20: second pass: the five unverified items

Closed the five gaps the first pass left open: Policy v2 in the contract, the exercised features, the connector release path, the untriggered error branches, and the retired flag. Each change has a test or a run named in [COVERAGE.md](COVERAGE.md#verification-log).

Code and contract changes:

- The 28 Policy v2 operations (`/v2/decisions`, `/v2/register/*`, `/v2/reviews/*`, `/v2/evidence/*`, `/v2/console/*`, `/v2/notifications/*`) are in the OpenAPI document, tagged _Policy v2 (experimental)_ and marked `x-stability: experimental`. Their cURL, TypeScript and Python samples are generated by `scripts/openapi/generate-policy-v2-samples.ts`, which `npm run openapi` runs.
- The route-parity test mounts the Policy v2 routes, so the document and the server are compared for them too.
- A new HTTP test pins the `500 EXECUTION_RECORD_INCOMPLETE` branch: the action runs once, and the response has the code and the transaction id.
- Tutorial 81 states the environment it needs. Its README command failed without it.
- The retired `PARMANA_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED_POLICY` is removed from the Docker workflow and the outage drill. Its unit test now asserts that the flag has no effect.

Portal changes: the Policy v2 statements that said "not in the OpenAPI document" were corrected. The error-code total is 106 (it was written as 105). The error-code rows for `202`, `500` and `502` name the test that triggers each one. The coverage report's untriggered list now records what was exercised, with the database-gated suites run against a local PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster.

Open, and new: the Policy v2 document format (F15), the open register response schemas (F16), and no live policy v2 server run (F17). The Docker stack and cloud deployment are still not run (F8).

## 2026-11-20: production-readiness pass on the code and the portal

Changed the code where the review had a verified defect, and corrected the portal to match. Every change has a test or a live check named in [COVERAGE.md](COVERAGE.md#known-issues-found-during-this-review). Items that need an owner's decision are in [FINDINGS.md](FINDINGS.md).

Code changes:

- `GET /version` and the API manifest report the `@parmana/api` package version (4.1.1), not a hand-typed `0.4.0`.
- Unknown routes return a JSON `404` with `code: ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`, not an HTML page.
- The installed `parmana-ops` command runs when started through its bin name. The fix is in the repository; a release containing it is needed.
- Hybrid signing is refused at start-up unless `SECONDARY_SIGNATURE_PROVIDER` is set and differs from the primary.
- Production refuses memory storage at start-up (the default when `PARMANA_STORAGE` is unset). This reverses an earlier test's expectation; the owner should confirm it ([FINDINGS F0](FINDINGS.md#f0-production-with-memory-storage-is-now-refused-a-reversal-to-confirm)).
- `scripts/generate-approver-key.ts` creates its output folder.
- The retired `PARMANA_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED_POLICY` flag is removed from the examples runner, the load test and tutorial 81.
- The TypeScript workspace test script runs with the root configuration, and the six empty test files are removed. `npm test --workspace=typescript` passes with no extra environment.
- Corrected comments: the schema 3 gate in `Config.ts`, and the `PARMANA_KEY_DIR` requirement in `.env.example`.
- Tutorials 60, 103 and 120 state the environment they need.
- The existing quickstart page is corrected: the policy and key directories, and a warning about the approval step.

Portal changes: every statement that described a fixed defect was updated, and the generated error reference and `llms-full.txt` were regenerated.

Open, and not changed (see [FINDINGS.md](FINDINGS.md)): the schema 2 default (F1), the SDK's legacy-record result (F2), the dev setup (F3), Python `version` versus TypeScript `version()` (F4), two `0.1.0` packages (F5), the Policy v2 contract (F6), approval automation (F7), the Docker, database and load checks (F8, F9), the Python and Node verifier test-count difference (F10), third-party reading of schema 3 (F11), the declared-transaction approval rule (F12), and unknown routes without a key (F13).

## 2026-11-20: first version of the developer portal

Added the developer portal in `docs/developer-portal/`, written from the repository's source and checked against it:

- **Portal structure:** overview, getting started, architecture, SDKs, REST API, tutorials, policy management, deployment, security, troubleshooting, reference, FAQ, glossary, examples, and this changelog.
- **SDK references:** `@parmana/sdk` (58 methods) and `parmana` (50 methods), each with a generated method index that gives every signature and the HTTP request each method sends. Also the offline verifier (`@parmana/verifier`, `parmana-verifier`), the operator CLI (`@parmana/cli`), and the connector SDK's contract.
- **REST API:** authentication, headers, errors, status codes, and the core endpoints with `curl`, JavaScript and sample responses. A generated index lists all 66 OpenAPI operations.
- **Tutorials:** Node.js, Python, fintech, refund authorization, maker-checker, transaction limits, AI agents, and evidence verification.
- **Security:** what is signed, canonical JSON and hashing, trust roots, schema versions and their coverage, tamper results, fail-closed behaviour, key management, and a production checklist.
- **Runnable examples:** a governed quickstart kit (setup script, TypeScript and Python flows, approval and limit cases, a REST smoke test, and a standalone verification script). Each was run against a local server for this release.
- **Tools:** `tools/generate-indexes.mjs` regenerates the method, endpoint and error-code indexes from source. `tools/check-docs.mjs` checks links and anchors, reports public methods and operations not named in narrative pages, and flags removed claims.
- **Coverage report:** [COVERAGE.md](COVERAGE.md), with the verification log, sixteen known issues found during this review, and the remaining gaps.

Documented findings that need an owner decision (none were changed in the repository):

- The existing quickstart does not run as written.
- The server reports version `0.4.0` while the packages are `4.1.1`.
- The installed `parmana-ops` binary prints nothing.
- Schema version 2 records leave most fields outside the signature. Schema version 3 is opt-in.
- A stale comment in the configuration describes schema version 3 as unreadable by the SDKs. Those SDKs read it correctly.
- The TypeScript workspace's `npm test` fails: six test files are empty.

Not changed: the server, the packages, the existing documentation site (`docs/site/`), the existing guides, the tests and the examples. The portal is not published, and the proposed navigation for the documentation site is not applied.

# Documentation coverage and verification report

[Portal home](README.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Known issues](#known-issues-found-during-this-review)

This report says what was documented, what was checked, what was run, what failed, and what remains. It was produced on **2026-11-20** from the parmana-core checkout on branch `ccr-ead4b602-t6o6n7`. The checkout's HEAD commit before this work was `1845194`. Every result below was observed in that run. Nothing is reported as passing that was not run.

## Summary

| Measure                                     | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Portal files                                | 38 Markdown files (34 narrative, 4 generated), plus 9 example files and 2 tools                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| TypeScript SDK methods documented           | **58 of 58** named in narrative pages, with signature and HTTP request for each in the generated index                                                                                                                                                            |
| Python SDK methods documented               | **50 of 50** named in narrative pages, with HTTP request for each in the generated index                                                                                                                                                                          |
| OpenAPI operations documented               | **94 of 94** named in narrative pages; **56** have a TypeScript SDK method that sends the same request, the other 38 are called over HTTP                                                                                                                         |
| Error codes indexed from source             | **106**, each with the file that raises it; **8** observed in a response or runner output                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Environment variables documented            | **All 65** names the code reads are in the [reference](reference/environment-variables.md): 54 in the server, SDK and CLI tables, and 11 script, test and tooling names in their own table                                                                        |
| Links                                       | **476 checked, all resolve** (the final check run is in the [verification log](#verification-log))                                                                                                                                                                |
| Examples run                                | **All 9** governed-quickstart files ran and passed in their stated configuration; the repository's own examples ran through `npm run examples` (116 examples, exit 0)                                                                                             |

## Missing examples

- A live refund against a server with a registered payment source. Tutorial 129 runs the decision in-process; the server path was not run.
- A run of each of the 202, 500 and 502 branches, and of `reconcile`.
- The approval of an external connector and of a signal source is covered by connector_and_signal_source.py, run on one network only: on a network where the endpoint does not resolve to a public address, the server refuses the approval, and the example prints that outcome.
- A bulk trust-record export example.
- Examples for `KEY_PROVIDER=aws-kms` and the secrets provider.
- Any example in a language other than TypeScript, Python or the shell. The repository has no Java or Go SDK; the API manifest lists them as `null`.

## Terminology

- The portal uses **Business Transaction**, **Execution Trust Record**, **policy version in effect**, **approval artifact** and **maker-checker** throughout, as the glossary defines them.
- The repository uses both "Trust Record" and "Execution Trust Record". The portal uses "Execution Trust Record" in full at first mention on each page, and "record" after that.
- The API says "approval", the schema says `approvalArtifact`, and the SDK calls the function `signApproval`. The portal uses "approval" in prose and the exact names in code.
- The API's `status` values (`RECEIVED`, `EXECUTING`, `VERIFIED`, and others) are plain strings in the Python SDK in this build.

## Remaining gaps

1. The Docker stack, PostgreSQL migrations and the cloud deployment were not run. The Docker path needs a host with a running daemon.
2. No latency or throughput figure is published. The load-test script was not run.
3. Backup, restore, rotation and KMS verification were described from scripts and code, not run.
4. The Python SDK's async behaviour is not applicable (the client is synchronous); the portal says so.
5. The TypeScript SDK in a browser is not documented, and is not verified.
6. The website navigation (see below) is proposed, not applied.

## Website integration

The repository's documentation site is Mintlify (`docs/site/docs.json`). This portal does not change that site. It is plain Markdown, and the [portal index](README.md#proposed-website-navigation) proposes a navigation. **Publishing or changing the site needs the owner's approval, and was not done.**

## Recommended next steps

1. Publish a `@parmana/cli` release that contains the entry-point fix (item 5), and then drop the workaround from the CLI pages.
2. Decide F1 (the schema 3 default) and F2 (the SDK fail-closed option), with the owner.
3. Decide F3 and F6, the dev setup and the Policy v2 contract.
4. Decide F5 (publish or privatise the two `0.1.0` packages).
5. Run the Docker stack, the migrations and the load test on a host with a daemon, and record the results (F8, F9).
6. Keep the governed kit in CI, since it is the only path in the portal that runs end to end.
